TEST-055/TEST-056 (acceptance-tests.md:68-69) make it checkable. Independent spot-checks of other high-risk terms hold up: AC-008 (requirements.md:73) pins the standing-record location per profile ('ux-spec.md' full / 'design.md' lite), and AC-009 (requirements.md:75-78) pins 'first occurrence' to the (feature, destination) pair with an explicit mechanism, not the word 'once' alone. No remaining term/state left underspecified enough for two implementers to diverge.

The round-1/round-2 Critical (fallback bullet writing the literal key 'ds_upload_consent', which trips TEST-021's no-'consent'-substring rule) is resolved by the indirect-reference ruling in AC-022 (requirements.md:165-167) and enforced by TEST-046 (acceptance-tests.md:60, negative check for the literal identifier) plus TEST-050 (acceptance-tests.md:64, general substring sweep). AC-003's absence default (requirements.md:35-37, resolves to per-feature) and AC-031's out-of-domain default (requirements.md:43-46, also per-feature) are consistent, not conflicting -- both fail toward the same safe outcome for a documented, shared reason (requirements.md:45). Edge Cases 1-9 (requirements.md:220-228) cover mid-life setting changes, pre-existing DS-29-era records, once-scoping, host-absence under both off and standing, a live human answering the per-feature prompt after standing is later set, .ps1 divergence, and a negative-assertion false-positive risk. The round-1 gap is now Edge Case 10 (requirements.md:229): present-but-out-of-domain value, resolved by AC-031 and tested by TEST-055/TEST-056 (acceptance-tests.md:68-69, elaborated at :95-97). No further material negative path (e.g., malformed AGENTS.md table, concurrent-session write races) is implied by the requirements as document-conformance-testable, so none is missing.

The Assumptions section (requirements.md:231-237) marks each item as re-verified-at-drafting-time-and-must-be-re-derived-at-implementation, an explicit non-blocking re-verification instruction rather than a silent assumption. Open Questions (requirements.md:250-256): OQ-1 and OQ-3 are marked Resolved with dated coordinator rulings recorded in the Resolutions section (requirements.md:258-262); the remaining OQ-2/OQ-4/OQ-5 are explicitly flagged non-blocking under 'Still open' (requirements.md:273), each hedged by a named acceptance criterion (AC-019 for OQ-2) rather than left ungoverned.

The consent-resolution boundary itself (per-feature live prompt / standing audit-only skip / off persistent forbiddance) is fully testable: AC-007-AC-014 (requirements.md:67-105) plus TEST-008-TEST-018 (acceptance-tests.md:22-32) exercise every branch. The separate, narrower gap -- no technical distinction between a human and an agent setting ds_upload_consent: standing in an unguarded AGENTS.md -- is explicitly disclosed as an accepted residual risk, not glossed over: requirements.md:13-15 states it plainly ('the specification must say plainly what is traded'), and Non-goals (requirements.md:214) records it as a deliberate scope exclusion with reasoning ('adding a guard... is a larger change than this issue asks for'). A disclosed, reasoned scope limit on an inherently non-document-verifiable fact (who authored a line) is not the same failure mode as an untestable approval boundary silently left ambiguous.

Every REQ carries AC(s) with resolution mechanics and a corresponding TEST row (acceptance-tests.md Test Matrix, TEST-001-TEST-056), and the round-2/round-3 coordinator rulings (requirements.md:258-269, including round-3 ruling F for AC-031) close prior open items without requiring a downstream reviewer to invent product behavior. Remaining open items (OQ-2, OQ-4, OQ-5) are explicitly marked non-blocking (requirements.md:273) and each is hedged by a named criterion rather than deferred silently.
